messages.subject: Very long compilation time for Stan ODE model -- possibly hanging?

So reading previous threads in this Google Group, it looks like long compilation times should be expected for models longer than 10 lines, but I've been waiting for 2 hours for a model to compile at the "INFO:pystan:COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL anon_model_6660a7a15aa3be82d76316518ba42209 NOW " message, and I'm wondering if it just hung, or whether I should be patient. I am currently using a 2014 Macbook Air with 8 GB of Ram and an i7 (probably a Haswell).

I'm currently using PyStan and have attached the scripts and data I am working with.

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Re: Very long compilation time for Stan ODE model -- possibly hanging?
parts:
I had a similar problem recently and 'hanging' was caused by the integrator getting stuck for high parameter values. To solve this I put upper bounds on parameters which helped. I know this isn't ideal since we want to avoid using these sorts of ``cutoff'' priors, but thought I'd let you know what helped me.

I see that you have quite a few parameters that have no upper bounds; perhaps try putting upper limits on them?

I think this issue is going to be fixed for the next release of Stan (2.10.0); however someone in the know please correct me if I'm wrong.

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Very long compilation time for Stan ODE model -- possibly hanging?
parts:
You can set refresh=1 to see if things are really hung
before the first iteration.

Stan 2.10 is about to be released which should fix a lot of
issues with hanging ODE solvers. The non-stiff solvers will have
a cap on number of iterations and we'll have stiff solvers. Right
now, the solver can go into what's effectively an infinite
loop.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Very long compilation time for Stan ODE model -- possibly hanging?
parts:
I was always suspicious about my initial conditions since they were so huge, and it turns out indeed I used the wrong numbers. I tried plugging in some dummy small numbers, but that still has not seemed to resolve the issue. Anyhow, I have attached my slightly updated code.

Putting in "refresh=1", I still see nothing in addition to the "COMPILING THE C++ MODEL" statement after hours of waiting -- should I take this to mean that the integrate_ode statement is getting stuck? Of course, I am suspicious of my own code, and wonder if there was another error that was not initially caught. Also, I am not sure if this signifies that my computer is getting overwhelmed? Looking at my Activity Monitor, I do see Python (Not Responding).

If someone could help me take a look at this again, that would be great. I am just not sure integrate_ode is the issue here. Thanks for the help and I have attached all necessary files to run this.

If this is indeed an issue that would be resolved by 2.10, I am thinking of then coding a Metropolis Hastings script as a first pass to get my advisor some initial results, and then to come back to Stan after 2.10 has been released.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Very long compilation time for Stan ODE model -- possibly hanging?
parts:
Yes, it's probably the integrator getting stuck if nothing
happens in an iteration. You can look at your process monitor
(depends on OS) to see how much memory's getting consumed --- another
possiblity is that you've started to swap.

We're rolling out Stan 2.10 soon, and that'll solve these problems.

- Bob
